---- MODULE W4Od6m1p3t3 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

Cars == {"e1", "e2", "e3"}
Calls == {"s1", "s2"}
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES token, owner, held, reqs
vars == <<token, owner, held, reqs>>

NextCar(e) == CASE e = "e1" -> "e2"
                [] e = "e2" -> "e3"
                [] e = "e3" -> "e1"

Init ==
    /\ token = "e1"
    /\ owner = [s \in Calls |-> NONE]
    /\ held = [e \in Cars |-> {}]
    /\ reqs = {}

Arrive(s) ==
    /\ s \notin reqs
    /\ owner[s] = NONE
    /\ reqs' = reqs \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, owner, held>>

Allocate(s) ==
    /\ s \in reqs
    /\ owner[s] = NONE
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = token]
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![token] = held[token] \cup {s}]
    /\ reqs' = reqs \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED token

Release(s) ==
    /\ owner[s] = token
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = NONE]
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![token] = held[token] \ {s}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, reqs>>

PassToken ==
    /\ token' = NextCar(token)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, held, reqs>>

SlowHold ==
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Calls : Arrive(s)
    \/ \E s \in Calls : Allocate(s)
    \/ \E s \in Calls : Release(s)
    \/ PassToken
    \/ SlowHold

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Cars
    /\ owner \in [Calls -> Cars \cup {NONE}]
    /\ held \in [Cars -> SUBSET Calls]
    /\ reqs \subseteq Calls

Coherent ==
    \A s \in Calls :
        owner[s] # NONE =>
            /\ s \in held[owner[s]]
            /\ \A e \in Cars : (s \in held[e]) => (e = owner[s])

NEXT Next
INVARIANT Coherent
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper coordinates which car answers each pending hall
call. To guarantee that no single call is ever answered by two cars at once, the
cars are arranged in a logical ring and pass a single access token around it.
Only the car currently holding the token may claim a call: it checks that the
call is still outstanding and unowned, then records itself as the owner both in
the shared dispatch table and in its own local set of assigned calls. A car may
release a call it owns, returning it to the free pool. New hall calls arrive over
time and join the outstanding-request set. Passing the token advances it to the
next car in the ring. Because a car may be slow but never failed, the token
holder is also allowed to simply hold the token idle for a step without acting;
this models a slow participant and never drops the token.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every owned call is recorded in exactly its owner car's local set and in no other car's set, so the dispatch table and the cars' local views never disagree about who holds a call.

Nodes == {"n1", "n2"}
NONE == "none"

vars == <<phase, votes, lock, inbox>>

    /\ votes = [i \in Ctrls |-> [n \in Nodes |-> NONE]]
    /\ lock = NONE
    /\ inbox = {}

Begin(i) ==
    /\ phase[i] = "idle"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![i] = "voting"]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![i] = [n \in Nodes |-> NONE]]
    /\ inbox' = {m \in inbox : m.ctrl # i}
    /\ UNCHANGED lock

CastVote(i, n, v) ==
    /\ phase[i] = "voting"
    /\ votes[i][n] = NONE
    /\ ~ \E m \in inbox : m.ctrl = i /\ m.node = n
    /\ inbox' = inbox \cup {[ctrl |-> i, node |-> n, v |-> v]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, votes, lock>>

Deliver(m) ==
    /\ m \in inbox
    /\ phase[m.ctrl] = "voting"
    /\ votes[m.ctrl][m.node] = NONE
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![m.ctrl][m.node] = m.v]
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, lock>>

Commit(i) ==
    /\ phase[i] = "voting"
    /\ \A n \in Nodes : votes[i][n] = "yes"
    /\ lock = NONE
    /\ lock' = i
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![i] = "held"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, inbox>>

Abort(i) ==
    /\ phase[i] = "voting"
    /\ \E n \in Nodes : votes[i][n] = "no"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![i] = "aborted"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, lock, inbox>>

Release(i) ==
    /\ phase[i] = "held"
    /\ lock = i
    /\ lock' = NONE
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![i] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, inbox>>

ResetAbort(i) ==
    /\ phase[i] = "aborted"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![i] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, lock, inbox>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Ctrls : Begin(i)
    \/ \E i \in Ctrls, n \in Nodes, v \in {"yes","no"} : CastVote(i, n, v)
    \/ \E m \in inbox : Deliver(m)
    \/ \E i \in Ctrls : Commit(i)
    \/ \E i \in Ctrls : Abort(i)
    \/ \E i \in Ctrls : Release(i)
    \/ \E i \in Ctrls : ResetAbort(i)

    /\ phase \in [Ctrls -> {"idle","voting","held","aborted"}]
    /\ votes \in [Ctrls -> [Nodes -> {NONE,"yes","no"}]]
    /\ lock \in Ctrls \cup {NONE}
    /\ inbox \subseteq [ctrl : Ctrls, node : Nodes, v : {"yes","no"}]

    /\ (lock # NONE => phase[lock] = "held")
    /\ \A i \in Ctrls : (phase[i] = "held") => (lock = i)

Two independent load-shedding controllers ("A" and "B") run over the same power
grid and must coordinate access to a single shared shed breaker that only one of
them may hold at a time. Each controller uses two-phase commit over the grid
nodes before it may seize the breaker: it opens a voting round, each node casts a
yes/no vote which travels as a message and is later delivered into that
controller's vote table, and only a unanimous yes lets the controller commit.
Committing seizes the breaker (the critical resource) but only if the breaker is
currently free; a controller that holds the breaker later releases it back to the
free state. A round with any no-vote aborts and is reset to idle.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The shared breaker is held by at most one controller at a time, and the breaker register always agrees with which controller is in its holding phase.

A network of vending machines draws from a single shared warehouse pool of at
most three refill units. Two independent restock controllers ("A" and "B") both
pull from this one pool, and each must win a quorum vote among the field agents
before it may draw units. A controller opens a collection round for a requested
amount, field agents cast approving votes one at a time, and once a majority
quorum of agents has approved, the controller may commit the draw -- but only if
the requested amount still fits within the remaining pool capacity. Committing
consumes that many units from the shared pool. A round that stalls can be
abandoned back to idle, and a completed round is reset so the controller can
start another.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The total number of units drawn from the shared pool never exceeds the pool capacity.

nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker allocates individual blood units to recipients.
Each unit may go to at most one recipient. To allocate a unit, a coordinator
opens an allocation round naming a still-free unit and a recipient, and a panel
of reviewers casts approving votes; once a majority quorum of reviewers approves,
the coordinator grants the unit to that recipient. A privileged administrator may
override the quorum and grant the pending unit immediately without waiting for
votes, but even the admin may only act on the unit named in the current round.
Any round -- whether it finished with a grant or stalled -- can be reset back to
idle so a new round can begin. A unit that has been
allocated can later be released back to the free pool. A round is only ever
opened on a unit that is not already owned.
SAFETY PROPERTY: While an allocation round is in progress, the unit it targets is never already owned, so no unit is ever allocated to a second recipient.

NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker keeps one shared lobby record that several
players may update concurrently. Updates use optimistic locking with retry: a
player first reads the record's current version into a private snapshot, and may
later commit a change only if the record's version still matches the snapshot it
read. A successful commit bumps the version by one and appends the base version
it built on to the change history. If a player's snapshot has gone stale (the
record moved on since it read), its commit is refused and it must drop the
snapshot and retry with a fresh read. A player may also
abandon its snapshot without committing at any time. A privileged administrator may force an
update through without holding a snapshot, but the forced update still builds on
the record's current version and bumps it by one just like a normal commit.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The change history is gap-free and never repeats a base version -- the i-th committed change always built on version i-1 -- so no update was ever silently overwritten by another.

A library book reservation system hands out individual copy slots to patrons, and
each slot may be reserved by at most one patron. The number of loanable slots is a
capacity that changes at runtime as copies are added or withdrawn from
circulation. To reserve a slot, a clerk opens a reservation round naming a still-
free slot and a patron, but only while the count of already-reserved slots is
below the current capacity; a review panel then casts approving votes, and once a
majority quorum approves the clerk grants the slot -- provided the slot is still
free and capacity still permits. The librarian may change the capacity at any

released back to the free pool, and any round can be reset to idle.

---- MODULE W4Od3m0p0t0 ----
EXTENDS Integers

Banks == {"b1", "b2", "b3"}
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES lock, status, snap, ledger
vars == <<lock, status, snap, ledger>>

Init ==
    /\ lock = NONE
    /\ status = [b \in Banks |-> "idle"]
    /\ snap = [b \in Banks |-> NONE]
    /\ ledger = NONE

Read(b) ==
    /\ status[b] = "idle"
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![b] = "trying"]
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![b] = lock]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lock, ledger>>

Acquire(b) ==
    /\ status[b] = "trying"
    /\ snap[b] = NONE
    /\ lock = NONE
    /\ lock' = b
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![b] = "cs"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, ledger>>

Retry(b) ==
    /\ status[b] = "trying"
    /\ snap[b] # lock
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![b] = lock]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lock, status, ledger>>

Exit(b) ==
    /\ status[b] = "cs"
    /\ lock = b
    /\ lock' = NONE
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![b] = "idle"]
    /\ ledger' = b
    /\ UNCHANGED snap

Crash(b) ==
    /\ status[b] # "crashed"
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![b] = "crashed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lock, snap, ledger>>

Recover(b) ==
    /\ status[b] = "crashed"
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![b] = "idle"]
    /\ lock' = IF lock = b THEN NONE ELSE lock
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![b] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED ledger

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Read(b)
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Acquire(b)
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Retry(b)
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Exit(b)
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Crash(b)
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Recover(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ lock \in Banks \cup {NONE}
    /\ status \in [Banks -> {"idle","trying","cs","crashed"}]
    /\ snap \in [Banks -> Banks \cup {NONE}]
    /\ ledger \in Banks \cup {NONE}

MutEx ==
    \A b \in Banks : (status[b] = "cs") => (lock = b)

====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT MutEx
nl:
Several banks share one interbank settlement batch that only one of them may be
posting to at any instant -- the batch ledger is a critical resource under mutual
exclusion. A bank enters the critical section using optimistic locking: it reads
the shared lock register into a private snapshot, and if that snapshot showed the
register free it attempts a compare-and-set that succeeds only while the register
is still free, at which point the bank is in the critical section. If the snapshot
has gone stale it must re-read and retry. On exiting, the bank clears the lock and
records itself as the last bank to post to the shared ledger. Any bank may crash silently at any time; a
crashed bank stops participating. A crashed bank may later reboot to idle, and if
it happened to be holding the lock when it crashed, rebooting also releases that
lock so others can proceed.
SAFETY PROPERTY: At any moment at most one bank is in the critical section, because a bank is in the critical section only when the shared lock register names it.
